overview.title: The world of the first Christians
overview.intro: The places that matter most in this era, from Jerusalem to Rome. Region names are the Roman ones used in Acts and Paul's letters.

journey-1.title: First journey
journey-1.intro: Acts says the church at Antioch sent out Barnabas and Paul. They crossed Cyprus, then went inland to cities in the Roman province of Galatia, in the regions Acts calls Pisidia and Lycaonia, and came back the same way.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Barnabas and Saul are sent out

journey-2.title: Second journey
journey-2.intro: Acts says Paul set out again with Silas, revisited the churches inland, then crossed by sea into Macedonia and Greece for the first time.

stops.name: Troas
stops.note: A vision of a man of Macedonia

stops.name: Caesarea
stops.note: He lands, then goes up to greet the church

journey-3.title: Third journey
journey-3.intro: Acts says Paul spent a long stay in Ephesus, went back through Macedonia and Greece, then sailed down the coast toward Jerusalem.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Paul sets out through Galatia and Phrygia

stops.name: Ephesus
stops.note: About two to three years; a riot

stops.name: Philippi
stops.note: After the days of Unleavened Bread

voyage.title: Voyage to Rome
voyage.intro: Acts says Paul, now a prisoner, was sent to Rome by ship. A storm drove the ship west for two weeks until it wrecked on Malta.

stops.name: Caesarea
stops.note: Paul is handed to a centurion

stops.name: Myra
stops.note: They change to a ship of Alexandria

stops.name: Malta
stops.note: Shipwreck; three months on the island

stops.name: Rome
stops.note: Two years under guard, still teaching

churches.title: Cities named in the sources for this era
churches.intro: The cities that appear most often in the writings of AD 100 to 313, from Antioch in the east to Carthage in the west. Lyons and Vienne in Gaul, where Irenaeus was bishop, lie off the western edge of this map.

ignatius.title: Ignatius on the road to Rome
ignatius.intro: Eusebius says Ignatius was sent from Syria to Rome under military guard, and that he wrote from Smyrna and from Troas. Polycarp's letter shows the Philippians had seen him pass. Nothing records the rest of the way, so the lines between these stops are straight and show only the order.

stops.name: Antioch
stops.note: Ignatius is bishop here and is sent to Rome

stops.name: Smyrna
stops.note: He meets Polycarp and writes to Ephesus, Magnesia, Tralles and Rome

stops.name: Troas
stops.note: He writes to Philadelphia, Smyrna and Polycarp

stops.name: Philippi
stops.note: Polycarp says the Philippians saw Ignatius, Rufus and Zosimus

stops.name: Rome
stops.note: He writes that he expects to face wild beasts here
